caption:
Manchester's tap water arrives at walking pace 💧
Much of it starts at Thirlmere in the Lake District and travels 153 km (about 95 miles) through Britain's longest gravity-fed aqueduct, with no pumps. It flows at about 6 km an hour and takes just over a day to reach the city. Opened in 1894, now topped up by Haweswater. United Utilities says most North West water is soft or very soft.

Where does your water come from? Comment your town 👇
Sources: Institution of Civil Engineers, Lake District National Park, United Utilities
